data.name: One Day in London
data.detailed_description:
The main characteristic of a visual novel game is achieving immersion by giving the player the ability to influence the story through choices. Every decision, every action the player-reader takes can drastically change the course of the story. The smallest detail can turn out to have an important role to play. In One Day In London you will solve puzzles, perform magical rituals, and carry out special tasks. A sophisticated achievement system will hint at alternative storylines, and a user-friendly save system allows you to move freely within this wonderful story to explore all possible branches.

ATTENTION! The main game includes only the first two chapters. Chapters III through V are sold separately as DLC.

Main features

  • nonlinear narrative, dozens of possible branching storylines;
  • several unique endings to the story you create yourself;
  • interactive gameplay, mini-games, quests;
  • memorable and well-written characters;
  • luxurious graphics, parallax, animated cut-scenes;
  • gorgeous soundtrack completely immerses you into the game;
  • exciting finale of the story you create!

The plot

The story is set in the 19th century England during Queen Victoria’s reign. Our main hero is a bored descendant of an aristocratic family who is fascinated by the occult. He becomes an initiate of a secret society by way of a friend’s invitation – and unexpectedly finds that legends are real. He faces the frightening underworld and becomes an unwilling participant in a series of weird events, sudden deaths, and underhanded machinations among humans, demons, and mystical creatures. Of course, a story can’t be complete without a mysterious lady whose past is shrouded in darkness… What outcome awaits our hero? Only time knows… Time and the player’s choice.

Disclaimer

The administration is not responsible for accidental summoning of any supernatural creature during the game.

reviews.review:
One Day in London is a story-rich visual novel that combines supernatural horror, detective fiction, and historical fantasy into a compelling interactive adventure. Developed and published by Owl Studio, the game transports players to Victorian England, where ancient myths, occult rituals, and hidden conspiracies lurk beneath the elegance of London's high society. You assume the role of an aristocrat whose fascination with the paranormal unexpectedly draws him into a dangerous secret organization, setting the stage for an adventure filled with mystery, betrayal, and difficult choices. The premise immediately captures attention by blending authentic historical atmosphere with dark fantasy, creating a world that feels both familiar and unsettling.

The narrative is unquestionably the game's greatest strength. Rather than presenting a linear story, One Day in London thrives on player agency by allowing decisions to shape conversations, relationships, investigations, and ultimately the fate of its characters. Every choice feels meaningful, encouraging players to think carefully before committing to a particular course of action. This branching structure also gives the game considerable replay value, as different decisions unlock alternate scenes, unique story developments, and multiple endings. Instead of simply revisiting the same events, each playthrough has the potential to reveal hidden perspectives and new pieces of the larger mystery, rewarding players who enjoy exploring every narrative possibility.

The setting plays a major role in establishing the game's identity. Victorian London is portrayed as a city where science, superstition, and secret societies exist side by side. As the story unfolds, mysterious murders, forgotten legends, magical rituals, and supernatural entities gradually become intertwined with the protagonist's personal journey. The game carefully builds suspense, introducing clues at a steady pace while withholding key revelations until the right moments. Along the way, players encounter a cast of memorable characters, including allies with uncertain motives and enigmatic figures whose pasts conceal important truths. The interactions between these characters help maintain emotional investment while adding depth to the central mystery.

Although One Day in London is primarily a visual novel, it incorporates several gameplay elements that prevent the experience from becoming entirely passive. Players will encounter puzzles, investigation sequences, hidden-object challenges, magical rituals, and small interactive activities that complement the storytelling. These moments provide welcome variety between lengthy dialogue scenes and reinforce the feeling that players are actively participating in the investigation rather than simply reading through it. The game also includes an accessible save system that makes experimenting with alternate decisions far less tedious, allowing players to revisit important moments without restarting the entire adventure.

Presentation is another area where the game performs well. The hand-crafted artwork successfully captures both the beauty and darkness of Victorian London, with detailed backgrounds, expressive character portraits, and eerie supernatural imagery that strengthen the gothic atmosphere. Animated scenes and visual effects give important moments additional impact, while the soundtrack enhances both suspenseful investigations and emotional conversations. The combination of visuals and music consistently supports the storytelling, creating an immersive environment that keeps players invested throughout the adventure.

One aspect prospective players should keep in mind is that the base game serves as the opening portion of a larger narrative, with later chapters released separately as downloadable content. While the initial chapters establish the characters, setting, and central conflict effectively, those seeking a completely self-contained story may be disappointed that the broader narrative continues beyond the base game. Even so, the opening chapters provide enough intriguing mysteries and satisfying character development to justify continuing the journey, especially for players who become invested in uncovering the truth behind London's supernatural secrets.

The pacing occasionally slows due to lengthy dialogue and extensive exposition, which is common within the visual novel genre. Players who prefer constant action may find certain conversations overly detailed, while completionists should be prepared to revisit familiar scenes when pursuing every branching path. Fortunately, the quality of the writing, the engaging world-building, and the consistently intriguing mystery help offset these slower moments, making the overall experience rewarding for those who appreciate narrative-focused adventures.

Overall, One Day in London successfully blends historical fiction, supernatural suspense, and interactive storytelling into a memorable visual novel. Its emphasis on meaningful choices, multiple endings, engaging investigations, atmospheric presentation, and rich Victorian setting creates an experience that stands above many conventional visual novels. While the chapter-based structure and slower pacing may not appeal to every player, fans of mystery, occult fiction, and branching narratives will find plenty to enjoy. Owl Studio delivers a captivating opening to an ambitious supernatural saga that encourages exploration, rewards curiosity, and leaves players eager to uncover every secret hidden within London's shadowy streets.

Rating: 8/10
